privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What The Nahwi stores and measures: no accounts, no cookies, no tracking across sites.
privacy.intro: The Nahwi has no accounts and sets no cookies.
privacy.device: Your progress, the madrasa path you chose, your practice answers, when each lesson is due for review, how many tests you take each day and your daily goal, your choices for the theme, the transliteration, the vowel marks and the typeface, and the date of the newest news you have seen (to mark what is new) are kept in your browser's local storage. They never leave your device. Clearing your browser data removes them.
privacy.offline: So that you can read offline, the site saves the course, the texts and the pages you have read in your browser's cache.
privacy.stats: To see which pages are used, we count page views with Vercel Web Analytics. It uses no cookies, does not follow you to other sites, and does not store your IP address; visits are counted in aggregate only. The fonts are served from this site, so your browser does not contact Google or any other font service. The “Google Translate” buttons under the old texts send that passage to Google Translate only when you click them.
privacy.contact: What you write in the contact form (your name, email address, subject and message) is sent by email to {email}, through the mail service Resend, so that we can read and answer it. It is not stored on this site and not used for anything else.
privacy.errors: If a script on a page goes wrong in your browser, a short report is sent to the site so that we can repair it: the page, the error message, where in the script it happened and the name of your browser. It holds nothing about you, not even your IP address, is kept only in the server log for a short time, and is not used for anything else.
privacy.descriptionAccounts: What The Nahwi stores and measures: optional accounts kept in the EU, no cookies, no tracking across sites.
privacy.introAccounts: The Nahwi sets no cookies. An account is optional: everything that is open stays open without one, and your progress then simply stays on this device.
privacy.deviceAccounts: Your progress, the madrasa path you chose, your practice answers, when each lesson is due for review, how many tests you take each day and your daily goal, your choices for the theme, the transliteration, the vowel marks and the typeface, and the date of the newest news you have seen (to mark what is new) are kept in your browser's local storage. They stay on your device unless you sign in (see below). Clearing your browser data removes them from this device.
privacy.hearts: Your hearts (how many tests you can take now, and when the next comes back), which questions your last test of each lesson asked, and whether a lesson is to be read again are kept there too. With an account your hearts are also kept with it, so they are the same on every device; a refill bought with Paddle is written there.
privacy.account: When you sign in, with your email address or with Google, your account keeps your email address, the scores of your tests, the steps you have seen and the madrasa path you chose, so that you can continue on another device. If you sign in with Google, Google also gives us your name and the address of your profile picture; we ask for nothing more. The account is stored with Supabase in the European Union (Frankfurt), which also keeps a log of sign-ins (time and IP address) for security for a limited time; the sign-in mails are sent through Resend. Your session is kept in your browser's local storage, not in a cookie. On your account page you can download everything stored about you, or delete your account, which removes it and everything in it at once.
privacy.accountApple: If you sign in with Apple, Apple gives us only your email address, or, if you choose to hide it, an address of Apple's that forwards our mails to you; it does not pass on your name.
privacy.accountPassword: If you set a password, Supabase keeps only a scrambled form of it (a hash), never the password itself; we cannot see it.
privacy.supportStore: To ask for support now and then, and never often, your browser also keeps how many pages you have read here and when the site last asked; nothing of it leaves your device.
privacy.app: When you open The Nahwi from its Android app, the site notes this for the session (in your browser's session storage), so that the app shows no payments; Google Play allows payments in an app only through its own billing. It is forgotten when the app is closed.
privacy.appIos: In the iPhone app, the daily reminder and the note that your hearts are full again are set on your phone, at the time you chose; the app also remembers your language for its next start. None of this leaves your phone.
privacy.accountCodes: If you redeem an access code, your account also keeps the access it gives and which code it came from, so that a code serves each account once, and for a week how many codes were tried each day (at most ten), against guessing. A code from a link (?redeem= or ?discount=) is kept in your browser's session storage until you use it or close the browser.
privacy.comments: If you write a question or remark under a lesson, your account keeps the message, the name you give (or that you chose to write without one), the lesson and the language. A moderator reads it before it is published; once published, everyone sees the message with the name you gave, or as “a learner”, but never your email address. You can delete a message at any time, and deleting your account deletes all of them.
privacy.payments: Full access is sold by Paddle, the merchant of record, under Paddle's own privacy policy: Paddle handles your payment details, billing address and receipts, and we never see your card number; in Paddle's dashboard we see what a seller needs, such as your email address, your country and your payments. To show the price for your country, the pricing page and the subscribe window load Paddle's script from Paddle's servers, which see your IP address. Your account keeps only what full access needs: the number of your subscription, its status and dates, and Paddle's links to cancel it or change how you pay. Deleting your account removes these from our side; Paddle keeps its records of payments for as long as the law requires.
privacy.appStore: In the iPhone app, full access is bought through Apple. RevenueCat, which handles these purchases for us, receives your account's number (a random id, not your name or address) and what you bought; Apple handles the payment, and we never see your payment details. Your account keeps the same as for a subscription on the website: its number, status and dates, and Apple's link to manage it.
privacy.gifts: A gift through the support button is paid on Stripe's own page, under Stripe's privacy policy; the site itself stores nothing of it.

terms.description: The terms for using The Nahwi, its free account and its paid full access.
sections: The service

The Nahwi (thenahwi.com) is a website for studying ṣarf and naḥw, the classical Arabic grammar of the madrasa: an encyclopedia that is open to everyone, and a study portal with courses, texts and tests. It is run by {owner}. You can reach us at {email}.
Accounts

An account is optional. You sign in with your email address or with Google. Keep access to your email account safe, since a sign-in mail opens your account. You can delete your account at any time on your account page.
Free and paid access

Without an account you can read the encyclopedia and three preview lessons in every book. A free account also opens the whole of al-Mabādiʾ. Full access, a paid subscription, opens every path, book and level. A madrasa or teacher can buy access for a class. Full access is a subscription, monthly or yearly, which renews until you cancel it. Lifetime access bought before 25 November 2026 stays valid for as long as the site runs; we cannot guarantee the future, but we will do our best to keep the site going and to support you.
Payment

Our order process is conducted by our online reseller Paddle.com. Paddle.com is the Merchant of Record for all our orders. Paddle provides all customer service inquiries and handles returns and refunds. Prices include any VAT or sales tax and may differ by country. A subscription renews at the end of each period until you cancel it.
Cancelling and refunds

You can cancel your subscription at any time; your access continues until the end of the period you have paid for, and no part of a period is refunded. We do not give refunds ourselves: refunds are handled by Paddle under its refund policy (paddle.com/legal/refund-policy), including any right of withdrawal that the law of your country gives you. See the refund policy. Lifetime access is not a subscription: there is nothing to cancel.
The content

The explanations, translations and tests are written for study and are drafts until reviewed by a qualified teacher; each lesson says whether it has been reviewed. They do not replace a teacher. The old texts are given from public-domain prints; our translations, explanations and tests belong to The Nahwi. You may quote them for study and teaching with a reference to the site, but not copy the courses as a whole or offer them elsewhere.
Fair use
Do not share your account, try to get around the access rules, or put an unreasonable load on the site. We may close an account that does.
Changes and availability

We keep the site running as well as we can, but cannot promise that it is always available or free of mistakes. We may change these terms; for a change that matters to subscribers we tell you by email beforehand.
Liability and law

As far as the law allows, The Nahwi is not liable for indirect damage from using the site. Dutch law applies. If you live in the European Union, the consumer law of your own country also protects you.

diagram.scSarfSub: its form: the word on its own
diagram.scNahwSub: its ending: the word in the sentence
diagram.kSpeechSub: words joined into a complete statement
diagram.shWeakSub: a wāw, yāʾ or alif: qāla, ramā

cap.sciences.all: Ṣarf studies the word on its own, naḥw the word in the sentence.
cap.sciences.sarf: Ṣarf: the form of the word on its own, its root and pattern.
cap.sciences.nahw: Naḥw: the word in the sentence, its role and its ending.
cap.kalima.all: Every word is a noun, a verb or a particle; words joined into a complete statement are speech.
cap.kalima.kalima: The word divides into three kinds, and nothing falls outside them.
cap.kalima.kalam: Speech: words joined so that the meaning is complete.
cap.kalima.ism: The noun: a meaning without a time.
cap.kalima.fil: The verb: a meaning together with a time.
cap.kalima.harf: The particle: its meaning only appears with another word.
cap.mizan.all: Every word is weighed against faʿala: fāʾ, ʿayn and lām stand for its three root letters.
cap.mizan.mizan: The scale faʿala: fāʾ, ʿayn and lām stand for the first, second and third root letters.
cap.mizan.mujarrad: The bare form: root letters only.
cap.mizan.mazid: The augmented form: letters added to the root.
cap.fil.all: The verb has three forms: past, present and command.
cap.fil.madi: The past tense: an act before the time of speaking.
cap.fil.mudari: The present tense: an act now or to come.
cap.fil.amr: The command: made from the present tense of the person addressed.
cap.sahih.all: A root is sound, or weak when it has a wāw, yāʾ or alif.
cap.sahih.sahih: The sound verb: no weak letter among its root letters.
cap.sahih.mutall: The weak verb: a wāw, yāʾ or alif among its root letters.
cap.mushtaqq.all: From one root: the act, the doer and the one acted on.
cap.mushtaqq.masdar: The verbal noun names the act itself.
cap.mushtaqq.fail: The active participle names the doer.
cap.mushtaqq.maful: The passive participle names the one acted on.
cap.irab.all: A word's ending changes (muʿrab) or stays (mabnī); the changes are rafʿ, naṣb, khafḍ and jazm.
cap.irab.irab: Iʿrāb: the ending changes with the governor.
cap.irab.bina: Bināʾ: the ending stays whatever governs the word.
cap.irab.anwa: The four states and their basic signs.
cap.jumla.all: A sentence begins with a noun or with a verb.
cap.jumla.ismiyya: The nominal sentence: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.
cap.jumla.mubtada: The mubtadaʾ: the noun the sentence begins with and speaks about.
cap.jumla.khabar: The khabar: what is said about the mubtadaʾ.
cap.jumla.filiyya: The verbal sentence: a verb, its doer and, if it takes one, an object.
cap.jumla.fail: The fāʿil: the doer after its verb.
cap.jumla.maful: The mafʿūl bihi: the one the act falls on.

about.title: About The Nahwi
about.description: What The Nahwi is, how its study paths work, who reviews it and who is behind it.
about.intro: The Nahwi is a place to learn ṣarf and naḥw, the Arabic grammar of the madrasa, from its own books, and to read about those books, their scholars and the curricula that order them.
about.teacherBody: A qualified teacher of Arabic grammar will review what The Nahwi teaches. Until a teacher has reviewed it, everything on the site, the explanations, the tests and the translations, is a draft.
about.teacherSource: From the tutors page of Madrasah Hanafiya
about.ownerBody: The Nahwi is made by {owner}, the owner of the project, who studies the Ḥanafī school.
parts: The encyclopedia: the handbooks of ṣarf and naḥw and a library of works by century, the scholars who wrote and taught them, the madrasa curricula, and news from the language sciences.

The study portal: three madrasa paths, read level by level, all opening with al-Mabādiʾ. The Indian path continues with the Persian primers of the Dars-i Niẓāmī, the Ottoman path with al-Amthila and Birgivī, and the North-African path with al-Ājurrūmiyya. Every lesson ends with a short test; the next one opens when you pass it.
about.nameBody: al-Naḥwī (النَّحْوِيّ) means “the grammarian”: the title the biographers give to the scholars of naḥw, from {sibawayh} to {ibnHisham}, as in the classic dictionaries of grammarians, the Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn.
about.textBody: The lessons follow the order of the books themselves, and the texts are given in the original, from public-domain prints named on every page, with our translations beside them. Your progress is kept on this device only.
about.contact: Questions, corrections or suggestions? Use the contact form.
about.parentBody: The Nahwi is a site of {mantiqi}, which teaches manṭiq, the logic of the madrasa, in the same way: the books of three madrasa paths, lesson by lesson, beside a free encyclopedia. In the madrasa the two were read side by side, so the two sites share their address, their accounts and their news: The Mantiqi gathers the news on naḥw and ṣarf each week, and you can write to both at {email}.

generations.title: The generations of the grammarians
generations.lead: The grammarians of naḥw and ṣarf by school and generation, as the old ṭabaqāt books set them out, and by the century they died in.
generations.description: The grammarians of Arabic by school and ṭabaqa after al-Zubaydī's Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn, and by century: their hijri year of death, city and books.
generations.introTitle: How the old books order the grammarians
intro: From the fourth/tenth century on, the grammarians wrote the history of their own science as ṭabaqāt, 'layers' or generations: the students of one generation's teachers form the next, so that a book of ṭabaqāt is a chain from the founder down to the author's own teachers. The oldest that survive were written within a few decades of each other: al-Sīrāfī's Akhbār al-naḥwiyyīn al-Baṣriyyīn, Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Lughawī's Marātib al-naḥwiyyīn and al-Zubaydī's Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn.

This page follows al-Zubaydī, who wrote in Cordoba at the command of the caliph al-Ḥakam II. He divides the scholars by city and by science: the grammarians of Basra in ten generations, from Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī to the students of al-Zajjāj; the grammarians of Kufa in six, from al-Ruʾāsī to the students of Thaʿlab; the lexicographers of both cities; then the men of Egypt, of Qayrawān and of al-Andalus. Each entry gives a scholar's teachers, books and the reports about him; the generations below, and the numbers of the entries, are his.

For the later centuries the ṭabaqāt go by name: Ibn al-Anbārī's Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ, al-Qifṭī's Inbāh al-ruwāt and al-Suyūṭī's Bughyat al-wuʿāt, which gathers more than two thousand grammarians and lexicographers down to the end of the ninth/fifteenth century. Here the grammarians after al-Zubaydī are set out by the school or land the histories place them in, with the books they wrote, down to the authors read on the three study paths.

madrasa.title: Choose your madrasa
madrasa.lead: Three paths through ṣarf and naḥw, level by level, following the books that the great madrasas read. All three open with al-Mabādiʾ; after it, every level has two lanes side by side, ṣarf and naḥw. Choose one to begin; you can change it at any time, and what you have passed stays passed.
madrasa.none: Choose a path above to see its levels.

indian.name: Indian madrasa
indian.lead: The Dars-i Niẓāmī of Farangī Maḥall, Deoband, Barelī and Khayrābād: Mīzān al-ṣarf beside Naḥw-i Mīr and the hundred governors, then Hidāyat al-naḥw, then al-Kāfiya with Sharḥ Jāmī and al-Shāfiya.

ottoman.name: Ottoman madrasa
ottoman.lead: Ṣarf first, as in the Ottoman, Syrian and Kurdish madrasas: al-Amthila, Bināʾ al-afʿāl and al-Maqṣūd; then al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ beside Birgivī's al-ʿAwāmil and Iẓhār al-asrār; then al-Kāfiya with Molla Câmî.

north-african.name: North-African madrasa
north-african.lead: Naḥw first: al-Ājurrūmiyya; then Qaṭr al-nadā beside al-ʿIzzī and Lāmiyyat al-afʿāl; then the Alfiyya: the grammar of al-Azhar, al-Qarawiyyīn, al-Zaytūna and the Mauritanian maḥāḍir.

indian-1.title: al-Mabādiʾ
indian-1.lead: The foundations of ṣarf and naḥw, term by term, free with an account: the word and its kinds, root and pattern, the tenses, iʿrāb and the sentence.

ottoman-1.title: al-Mabādiʾ
ottoman-1.lead: The foundations of ṣarf and naḥw, term by term, free with an account: the word and its kinds, root and pattern, the tenses, iʿrāb and the sentence.

north-african-1.title: al-Mabādiʾ
north-african-1.lead: The foundations of ṣarf and naḥw, term by term, free with an account: the word and its kinds, root and pattern, the tenses, iʿrāb and the sentence.

indian-2.title: Mīzān al-ṣarf and Naḥw-i Mīr
indian-2.lead: The Persian primers of the Dars-i Niẓāmī, read in the first year side by side: the scale faʿala and the patterns of the verb; the parts of speech, iʿrāb and the sentence, with ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī's hundred governors.

indian-3.title: Hidāyat al-naḥw
indian-3.lead: The Arabic handbook of naḥw read before al-Kāfiya in the Dars-i Niẓāmī: the noun, the verb and the particle, with their iʿrāb, in the order of al-Kāfiya.

indian-4.title: al-Kāfiya, Sharḥ Jāmī and al-Shāfiya
indian-4.lead: Ibn al-Ḥājib's two handbooks, the summits of naḥw and ṣarf, with Jāmī's commentary on al-Kāfiya.

ottoman-2.title: al-Amthila, Bināʾ al-afʿāl and al-Maqṣūd
ottoman-2.lead: Emsile, Binâ and Maksûd, the first books of the Ottoman madrasa, all ṣarf: the forms of naṣara set out, the building of the verbs, and the patterns of the bare and augmented verb.

ottoman-3.title: al-ʿIzzī, Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, al-ʿAwāmil and Iẓhār
ottoman-3.lead: Ṣarf goes on with al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, the weak verbs included; beside it naḥw begins, with Imām Birgivī's al-ʿAwāmil and Iẓhār al-asrār: the governors, the governed and iʿrāb.

ottoman-4.title: al-Kāfiya with Molla Câmî
ottoman-4.lead: Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Kāfiya with Jāmī's commentary, as read in the Ottoman madrasa.

north-african-2.title: al-Ājurrūmiyya
north-african-2.lead: Ibn Ājurrūm's short first book of naḥw, learnt by heart from the Maghrib to Java: speech, iʿrāb and its signs, the verbs, and the nouns in the nominative, accusative and genitive.

app.offlineBody: The Nahwi needs the internet the first time it opens. After that, the course, the terms and the practice open without it.
app.reminderBody: The app reminds you every day at the time you choose, with the number of lessons due for review. The reminders are set on your phone; nothing is sent to us.
app.reminderDenied: Notifications are off for The Nahwi. Turn them on in Settings → Notifications → The Nahwi, then try again.
app.notifyBody: Today's lesson is waiting for you.
app.notifyDue: Due for review today: {n}. A few minutes of tikrār keeps them fresh.
app.heartsBody: All five hearts are back: your next test is waiting.

store.loading: Loading the prices from the App Store…
store.unavailable: The App Store did not answer. Please try again in a moment.
store.fine: Payment is charged to your Apple ID when you confirm. A subscription renews automatically, every month or every year, unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the period; you can cancel it at any time in your Apple ID's settings, under Subscriptions.
store.thanks: Thank you! Your full access is being set up.
store.error: The purchase did not go through. Please try again, or write to us.
store.nothing: No purchase was found for this Apple ID.

parent.lineLong: The Nahwi is a site of {mantiqi}, the encyclopedia and study portal of manṭiq. The news, the address and the accounts are shared.
